title: C-Nash: A Novel Ferroelectric Computing-in-Memory Architecture for Solving Mixed Strategy Nash Equilibrium
problem: Nash equilibrium verification is NP-complete and computationally challenging. Existing quantum solvers only identify pure strategy NE solutions and fail to find mixed strategy NE solutions, leaving many solutions undiscovered.
motivation: Nash equilibrium concepts are pivotal in game theory with widespread applications across numerous industries, making efficient computation critical.
method: C-Nash combines ferroelectric transistors (special transistors that hold their state) with computing-in-memory to find Nash equilibrium solutions. The system converts the optimization problem into MAX-QUBO form (maximizing quadratic binary functions) without needing extra helper variables, uses a grid of ferroelectric transistors to store and directly compute on the game payoff matrices, and applies a winner-takes-all circuit with two-phase simulated annealing—a search method that explores solutions probabilistically before gradually narrowing the search—to find all equilibrium solutions.
key_novelty: A ferroelectric transistor architecture that solves both pure and mixed strategy Nash equilibrium without helper variables, enabling discovery of all equilibrium solutions.
contributions: MAX-QUBO transformation eliminating slack variables and objective function corruption
FeFET-based bi-crossbar hardware architecture for accelerated QUBO computations
Winner-takes-all and two-phase simulated annealing for comprehensive NE solution search
Complete coverage of pure and mixed strategy NE solutions versus partial quantum approaches

metrics.speedup: 157.9X vs D-Wave 2000 Q6; 79.0X vs D-Wave Advantage 4.1
metrics.accuracy: 68.6% improvement in NE discovery success rate; 100% coverage of pure and mixed solutions
